Ещё два документа едут вместе с кодом: docs/api-contract.md и apps/operator-panel/ARCHITECTURE.md.

/

    Start here. This is the plain-language map of the operator console: what it's for, who gets in, and every screen at a glance. For what each screen does and what each action does, read the staff playbook. For the technical wiring (how the frontend talks to /api), read the dev-facing ARCHITECTURE.md — apps/operator-panel/ARCHITECTURE.md in the code package.

    Rebuilding it? Read this box first

    Everything below assumes you can already see the console. These are the four things that decide whether you can, and none of them is discoverable from the documents.

    1 — The code came with these documents. One directory, offplan-operator/, and everything runs from it:

    npm ci
npm run dev                            # → http://localhost:5173/operator-next/

    Node 22+, npm not pnpm. Nothing resolves outside the archive and there is no environment variable to set. The dev server proxies /api/* to our live backend, so there is no backend to stand up. HANDOVER.md at the package root is the long version of this paragraph.

    2 — You need an operator account, and only we can issue one. The console admits only an active row in our operators table; no command creates one and no local flag bypasses it. Every screen past sign-in is unreachable without it. Send us the email addresses that need access, early — this is the single thing most likely to stall a first day. Sign-in is a magic link, no password.

    3 — You do not need a Cloudflare Access token. It is true of the studio dashboard and false of this console, which owns its own session on a different host. Nothing to configure, nothing to ask us for. If any file in the package still asks for one, it is describing the dashboard.

    4 — ⚠️ The data behind this console is live customer data. The dev server proxies /api to production. There is no seed database and no staging tenant: what you see is real studios, their real invoices and card state, the real email addresses of their users, and the audit trail of what our staff did to them. Under our controller/processor split that makes your developers processors of personal data on our behalf, so an account is issued against a signed NDA and DPA, not against a request — and it is issued at the cs role, which is read-plus-support and cannot suspend, delete, refund or change anyone's role. If a task genuinely needs a heavier role, ask for it for that task. Do not export, screenshot into a ticket, or paste customer rows anywhere outside the console.

    Then read in the order at the top of this page. The build order tells you when to open the two that travel with the code.

    Two comments in the code contradict the code. apps/operator-panel/ARCHITECTURE.md names the session cookie op_session in its opening section — the right name is op_admin_session, as the same file's roles table says lower down. And src/main.tsx describes route-level lazy chunk-splitting with vite:preloadError recovery; the router imports every route statically, so there are no chunks and that handler never fires. Both are comments only — the code itself is correct. Ask us for corrected copies.

    What it is

    The operator console is offplan.online's internal staff cockpit for running the business behind the product. Our customers are studios (the agencies/developers who publish sales pages); the console is where our own staff watch those studios' health, manage their billing and domains, read the audit trail of who-did-what, and administer staff access. It is a read-mostly monitoring + light-touch admin surface — most screens show you state; a handful let a manager act (extend a trial, freeze a project, invite a teammate).

    It is not a customer surface. It sits alongside two others:

    • Studio owners use the client dashboard (/dash) — their own projects.
    • Buyers/clients use the sales pages — the public property pages.
    • Staff (you) use this console (/operator-next) — everyone's studios, from above.

    Who's allowed in

    In plain terms: you sign in by email, and there is no password box. On the Sign in screen you enter your work address, clear a Turnstile check, and a single-use link valid for 30 minutes arrives by email; clicking it starts your session. The console lives at ops.offplan.online/operator-next/.

    Two things must both be true for you to get in: (1) the link you clicked is unspent and unexpired, and (2) you have an active server-side operator-staff account. Miss either and you land back on Sign in — which will never tell you which one you missed, on purpose: the reply is identical for an active operator, a deactivated one and a stranger, so the form cannot be used to discover who has console access. The playbook's Sign in section lists the four reasons the gate can send you there and what each one means.

    Your role decides which act affordances you see — but the server is the real authority; the UI only shows/hides. (Full auth model: the dev ARCHITECTURE.md — apps/operator-panel/ARCHITECTURE.md in the code package.)

    ⚠️ There is no SSO, and no Cloudflare Access in front of this console. No SSO button, no @offplan.online identity check at the edge, no Re-authenticate action — a grep for cf-access / CF_Authorization under the console's client source returns nothing. Worth stating plainly because the code package's README.md still asks for a Cloudflare Access token: that is true of the studio dashboard and false here. The console owns its own magic-link session (ADR 0048) on its own host (ADR 0047).

    The chrome you navigate by

    Every screen except the two public ones (Sign in, Verify sign-in link) sits inside one shell — OperatorLayout:

    • Topbar — the identity pill (your email + role) and global context.
    • Sidebar — the primary nav, grouped: Overview → Studios → Operations (Payments / Domains / Audit) → System (Operators / Settings).
    • CommandBar — quick navigation/search.

    This shell is chrome, not a screen — it wraps everything below and threads your identity + role down to the screens. (It's why it isn't a row in the screen table.)

    Screens at a glance

    The console has 20 screens you navigate to, grouped as the sidebar groups them. (The router declares 21 leaf routes — the twenty-first is NotFoundRoute, which nobody navigates to on purpose; the playbook counts it, this page does not.) One line each; the playbook has a full section per screen (and, at its top, the reconciled route → component → data-status table + a glossary of the recurring terms). Data column: WIRED = real/live data · PARTIAL = mostly real, one part still derived/placeholder · STUB = placeholder pending backend.

    Keeping this current

    These docs are only useful while they match the console people actually see, so there's a tripwire against structural drift — a screen added or removed without a matching doc entry:

    python3 scripts/check_docs_screens.py           # report (always exit 0)
python3 scripts/check_docs_screens.py --strict  # exit 1 on drift — for CI

    It compares the router's route table (router.tsx, the source of truth) against the playbook's per-screen <!-- route: --> markers and warns either way. The same guard runs in the test suite (python3 -m unittest tests.test_check_docs_screens). What it can't catch is semantic drift — a button whose effect changed while its route stayed put. That's what the last_reviewed: date on each doc is for: re-read on a cadence (the check prints each doc's review age), and bump the date when you do.

    Начинайте отсюда. Это карта операторской консоли обычным языком: для чего она, кого пускают и все экраны одной строкой. О том, что делает каждый экран и что делает каждое действие, читайте плейбук для сотрудников. Про техническую обвязку (как фронтенд разговаривает с /api) — в документе для разработчиков ARCHITECTURE.md, это apps/operator-panel/ARCHITECTURE.md в пакете кода.

    Переписываете её? Сначала прочитайте эту рамку

    Всё, что ниже, предполагает, что вы уже видите консоль. Вот четыре вещи, которые решают, увидите ли вы её, и ни одна из них не выводится из документов.

    1 — Код приехал вместе с этими документами. Один каталог, offplan-operator/, и всё запускается из него:

    npm ci
npm run dev                            # → http://localhost:5173/operator-next/

    Node 22+, npm, а не pnpm. Наружу архива ничего не резолвится, переменные окружения выставлять не нужно. Dev-сервер проксирует /api/* на наш живой бэкенд — поднимать бэкенд не нужно. HANDOVER.md в корне пакета является длинной версией этого абзаца.

    2 — Вам нужен операторский аккаунт, и выдать его можем только мы. Консоль пускает только по активной строке в нашей таблице operators; ни одна команда её не создаёт и ни один локальный флаг её не обходит. Без неё недостижим любой экран за входом. Пришлите нам адреса, которым нужен доступ, заранее — это то единственное, что с наибольшей вероятностью застопорит первый день. Вход по magic link, пароля нет.

    3 — Токен Cloudflare Access вам не нужен. Это верно для дашборда студий и неверно для этой консоли, у которой своя сессия на другом хосте. Настраивать нечего, просить у нас нечего. Если какой-то файл в пакете всё же его просит — он описывает дашборд.

    4 — ⚠️ За этой консолью живые данные клиентов. Dev-сервер проксирует /api в прод. Никакой посевной базы и никакого тестового арендатора нет: вы видите настоящие студии, их настоящие счета и состояние карты, настоящие почтовые адреса их пользователей и журнал того, что наши сотрудники с ними делали. По нашему разделению controller/processor это делает ваших разработчиков обработчиками персональных данных от нашего имени, поэтому аккаунт выдаётся под подписанные NDA и DPA, а не по запросу — и выдаётся с ролью cs: чтение плюс поддержка, без возможности заморозить, удалить, вернуть деньги или сменить кому-либо роль. Если задаче действительно нужна роль тяжелее — просите под эту задачу. Не выгружайте, не вставляйте скриншотами в тикеты и вообще не выносите строки с клиентами за пределы консоли.

    Дальше читайте в порядке, указанном вверху страницы. Порядок сборки говорит, когда открывать те два документа, что едут вместе с кодом.

    Два комментария в коде противоречат коду. В apps/operator-panel/ARCHITECTURE.md сессионная кука в начале названа op_session — верное имя op_admin_session, как и говорит таблица ролей ниже в том же файле. А src/main.tsx описывает пороутный lazy со восстановлением по vite:preloadError; роутер импортирует все роуты статически, так что чанков нет и этот обработчик не срабатывает никогда. Оба — только комментарии, сам код корректен. Исправленные копии — по запросу.

    Что это такое

    Операторская консоль — это внутренняя рубка сотрудников offplan.online для ведения бизнеса за продуктом. Наши клиенты — студии (агентства и застройщики, которые публикуют страницы продаж); консоль — это место, где наши собственные сотрудники следят за здоровьем этих студий, ведут их биллинг и домены, читают журнал «кто что сделал» и администрируют доступ сотрудников. Это поверхность преимущественно для чтения плюс лёгкое администрирование: большинство экранов показывают состояние, и лишь несколько позволяют управляющему действовать (продлить пробный период, заморозить проект, пригласить коллегу).

    Это не клиентская поверхность. Рядом с ней есть ещё две:

    • Владельцы студий пользуются дашбордом клиента (/dash) — своими проектами.
    • Покупатели и клиенты пользуются страницами продаж — публичными страницами объектов.
    • Сотрудники (вы) пользуются этой консолью (/operator-next) — всеми студиями, сверху.

    Кого пускают

    Простыми словами: вы входите по почте, и поля пароля нет. На экране Sign in вы вводите свой рабочий адрес, проходите проверку Turnstile, и на почту приходит одноразовая ссылка, действительная 30 минут; клик по ней начинает сессию. Консоль живёт по адресу ops.offplan.online/operator-next/.

    Чтобы вас пустили, должны быть верны одновременно две вещи: (1) ссылка, по которой вы кликнули, не потрачена и не просрочена, и (2) у вас есть активная серверная запись операторского аккаунта. Не выполнено любое из двух — и вы снова оказываетесь на Sign in, который никогда не скажет, какое именно, и это сделано намеренно: ответ одинаков для активного оператора, деактивированного и постороннего, поэтому форму нельзя использовать, чтобы выяснить, у кого есть доступ к консоли. Раздел Sign in в плейбуке перечисляет четыре причины, по которым гейт может вас туда отправить, и что каждая означает.

    Ваша роль решает, какие возможности действия вы видите, — но настоящим авторитетом является сервер; интерфейс лишь показывает и прячет. (Полная модель аутентификации — в ARCHITECTURE.md для разработчиков, это apps/operator-panel/ARCHITECTURE.md в пакете кода.)

    ⚠️ Никакого SSO нет, и Cloudflare Access перед этой консолью не стоит. Ни кнопки SSO, ни проверки принадлежности к @offplan.online на периметре, ни действия Re-authenticate — поиск cf-access / CF_Authorization по клиентскому исходнику консоли не находит ничего. Сказать это прямо стоит потому, что README.md в пакете кода до сих пор просит токен Cloudflare Access: для дашборда студий это верно, здесь — нет. У консоли собственная сессия на magic link (ADR 0048) на собственном хосте (ADR 0047).

    Хром, по которому вы навигируете

    Каждый экран, кроме двух публичных (Sign in, Verify sign-in link), находится внутри одной оболочки — OperatorLayout:

    • Топбар — пилюля личности (ваша почта и роль) и глобальный контекст.
    • Боковая панель — основная навигация, сгруппированная: Overview → Studios → Operations (Payments / Domains / Audit) → System (Operators / Settings).
    • CommandBar — быстрая навигация и поиск.

    Эта оболочка является хромом, а не экраном: она оборачивает всё нижеследующее и протягивает вашу личность и роль вниз, к экранам. (Поэтому её нет строкой в таблице экранов.)

    Экраны одним взглядом

    В консоли 20 экранов, на которые вы переходите, сгруппированных так же, как их группирует боковая панель. (Роутер объявляет 21 лист — двадцать первый это NotFoundRoute, на который никто не переходит намеренно; плейбук его считает, эта страница — нет.) По строке на каждый; в плейбуке на каждый экран есть полный раздел (а вверху — сверенная таблица маршрут → компонент → состояние данных плюс глоссарий повторяющихся терминов). Колонка данных: WIRED — настоящие живые данные · PARTIAL — в основном настоящие, одна часть всё ещё выводится или является заглушкой · STUB — заглушка в ожидании бэкенда.

    Operations

    Как это поддерживается в актуальном виде

    Эти документы полезны ровно до тех пор, пока совпадают с той консолью, которую люди видят на самом деле, поэтому есть растяжка против структурного расхождения — экран добавили или убрали, а записи в документах нет:

    python3 scripts/check_docs_screens.py           # отчёт (всегда код возврата 0)
python3 scripts/check_docs_screens.py --strict  # код 1 при расхождении — для CI

    Она сравнивает таблицу маршрутов роутера (router.tsx, источник истины) с маркерами <!-- route: --> в плейбуке и предупреждает в обе стороны. Та же проверка выполняется в наборе тестов (python3 -m unittest tests.test_check_docs_screens). Чего она поймать не может — это семантического расхождения: кнопка, у которой изменился эффект, а маршрут остался на месте. Ровно для этого в каждом документе есть дата last_reviewed: — перечитывать с некоторой периодичностью (проверка печатает возраст ревью каждого документа) и обновлять дату, когда перечитали.

    См. также

    • Плейбук для сотрудников — что делает каждый экран и каждое действие, плюс сверенная таблица маршрут → компонент → состояние данных (читать следующим).
    • Спецификация на переписывание — матрица ролей, приложение по данным и API, что строить иначе.
    • Порядок сборки — последовательность и во сколько обходится каждый кусок.
    • ARCHITECTURE.md для разработчиков — apps/operator-panel/ARCHITECTURE.md в пакете кода — обвязка фронтенд↔/api, для инженеров.

    What this is. A section per screen: what it is, what each action does, and what happens after. Read the index first for the map and access rules; this is the detail. Screen order matches the sidebar.

    Scope — capability, not policy. This tells you what a control does and what follows — e.g. "Extend trial adds N days and the studio's trial banner updates." It does not tell you when you should do it (that operational policy / SOP is separate, deferred work). Where an action is manager-only, the server enforces it and the button is simply hidden for non-managers (the client hide is defence-in-depth, not the authority).

    STUB marks a screen or action whose data is a placeholder not yet wired to a backend — it renders, but it isn't live.

    About the screenshots. All twelve were captured from the live console on 2026-08-17, so they agree with the text. Email addresses are masked — the console holds real customer data and these pages are published openly; operator1@offplan.online and studio-owner1@example.com are placeholders, consistently applied. Studio slugs are not masked: they are already public as <slug>.offplan.online.

    The route: HTML-comment under each heading (holding that screen's path) is machine-readable — the anti-rot check (scripts/check_docs_screens.py) matches those paths against router.tsx. Keep exactly one per screen.

    Terms & labels

    Recurring vocabulary, defined once. Skim this before the tables below.

    Data status (the right-hand column everywhere):

    Label Means
    WIRED Real data — the screen fetches and shows live values.
    PARTIAL Mostly real, but one part is still derived/placeholder (noted per screen).
    STUB Placeholder — it renders, but the data/action isn't connected to a backend yet.
    Phase-2 A control that's visible but deliberately disabled — not built yet (not broken).

    The rest:

    • chrome — the fixed frame around every screen (topbar + sidebar + command bar); not a screen itself. Sticky since 2026-08-15: the topbar and sidebar stay in view at any scroll depth, and table column headers stick under the topbar — unless a table is too wide to fit, in which case it drops to horizontal scroll with the identifier column frozen, so no column is ever unreachable and no row loses its name.
    • pill / badge — a small rounded status label (e.g. TRIAL, PAID, a health dot). Used interchangeably.
    • Magic link — how you sign in. You type your work email on the Sign in screen, clear a Turnstile check, and a single-use link valid for 30 minutes arrives by email; clicking it starts the session. There is no password box, and there is no SSO button — the email is the credential. (offplan's ADR 0048 is the decision behind the session; ADR 0047 is the separate one about the host it moved to.)
    • CF Access (Cloudflare Access) — retired 2026-07-31. Until then the console sat behind Cloudflare Access and sign-in happened at the edge, before the app loaded. No part of the console does this any more — a grep for cf-access / CF_Authorization under apps/operator-panel/src/app/ returns nothing. The term survives here only so that an older doc, ADR or commit message that mentions it can be read; if you are hunting for an SSO path, there isn't one.
    • ADR — an architecture decision record (the "why we did it this way" notes in docs/decisions/). When a screen says "per ADR 00NN", that's the rule behind the behaviour. The ADR files don't travel with this set, so the ones the console's code cites are here:
      • 0003 — soft-suspend is reversible; hard-delete is GDPR erasure.
      • 0004 — audit + buyer-record retention: 12 months, then actor identities hash (that job does not exist yet).
      • 0028 — subdomain rename policy + slug validation.
      • 0031 — pricing structure. Commercially out of scope for the rebuild.
      • 0034 — the studio tag taxonomy.
      • 0040 — delete governance: suspend-first, and a guarded delete is not an erasure.
      • 0048 — this console's own session on its own host (see Magic link above).
      • 0049 — the server decides what is permitted, not the panel (can() against ACTION_ROLES).
      • 0051 — non-payment: the page goes dark at period end and the restore window closes by derivation.
    • MRR / ARR — monthly / annual recurring revenue (the subscription-revenue KPIs on Payments).
    • keyset pagination — just page-by-page Prev / Next (no jump-to-page). You don't need the mechanism, only the buttons.
    • tombstone / 301 → 410 — a retired address kept on record after a rename: first it 301-redirects (moved) to the new one, then becomes 410 gone. Shown in domain history.
    • PII / pseudonymised / PII tier — PII = personal data. "PII tier" flags how sensitive a logged field is, and sensitive fields are stripped from the metadata before it is written. Pseudonymised is a plan, not a state: ADR 0004 says actor identities become a hash after 12 months, and the job that would do it does not exist — every actor in the log is stored and shown in cleartext regardless of age (audit.ts:6-8).
    • Copy view link — a control on all eight list consoles (Studios, Operators, Status, Studio users, Activity, Domains, Payments, Audit) that copies the current filtered view as an absolute URL. What each screen's filters put in the URL is a compatibility surface — parameters are added, never renamed (the authoritative per-screen table lives in the operator-panel ARCHITECTURE.md). Defaults are never written to the URL. Labels: Copy view link → Link copied (or Could not copy — use the address bar).
    • stale-parameter notice — when a pasted link carries a value a screen no longer recognises (a deleted tag, a retired filter), the screen shows the default view and says so in one sentence (e.g. tag "vip" no longer exists — showing the default view) instead of erroring or silently dropping it.
    • return path — a shared console link that forces a sign-in survives it: the destination is stashed locally (60 minutes, consumed once) and the magic-link verify drops you back on the exact filtered view. Not a ?next= parameter — nothing about the destination travels in the emailed link.
    • /dash — the studio's own client dashboard (a separate surface, not this console — see the index).
    • FEATURE_REGISTRY — the fixed, server-side catalogue of product features that the Projects "Features grid" toggles come from.
    • blast radius — on a freeze/suspend confirm, the count of what the action hits: how many projects go offline and how many are on paid plans.
    • "go dark" / freeze — a frozen project's public sales page stops serving to buyers (it's taken offline), until it's resumed.

    All screens

    The reconciled spine — every screen, its route, the React component + file behind it, and whether its data is real (WIRED) or a placeholder (STUB). Each row expands into a full section below. The router is the source of truth (apps/operator-panel/src/app/router.tsx); this table is reconciled against it (last done 2026-08-17) and the anti-rot check catches any drift.

    One date, not three. The frontmatter's last_reviewed is the only freshness claim this document makes. Dates that appear inside the dated notes below are the history of how it got here — read them as "what happened on that day", never as "how fresh this is".

    router.tsx declares 24 element-bearing nodes = 21 leaf screens + 2 layout wrappers + 1 auth gate. The layouts are chrome, not screens: OperatorLayout (/ — the topbar/sidebar/CommandBar shell, described in the index) and StudioHubLayout (studios/:slug — the shell for the 8 studio-hub tabs; kept as a row below for context). OperatorAuthGate is element-bearing too and used to go uncounted, which is how this paragraph read 21 for a router that declared 24. Paths are relative to the /operator-next basename. /signed-out and /auth/verify are public by necessity — they run before an identity exists; everything below them is gated by OperatorAuthGate on an op_admin_session cookie, and only that cookie (the CF Access header this sentence used to name has not been a path since 2026-07-31).

    ⚠️ One leaf below has no <!-- route: --> marker, on purpose. NotFoundRoute (path: "*", router.tsx:104) is excluded by the anti-rot check itself (check_docs_screens.py:221-224 — a catch-all renders the 404 fallback, not a documented screen), so giving it a marker would turn the check red for a doc that got more complete. It gets a spine row and no section. That is why the check reports 20 routes / 20 markers against 21 leaves.

    Where the retention table went. It used to sit on the Settings screen; it was four hardcoded strings and none of the four policies has an implementation, so it lives here instead — see Data-retention horizons below. Bring it back to Settings when a row is genuinely enforced.

    Data-retention horizons

    Policy, not configuration. Nothing in the product reads or enforces these yet.

    Policy Horizon Enforced Source
    Audit actor pseudonymise after 12 months No — no writer; actors stored in cleartext ADR 0004
    Buyer (unconverted) retention 24 months No — no purge job ADR 0004 v3
    Buyer (converted) retention 7 years No — no purge job ADR 0004 v3
    Impersonation token TTL 30 minutes No — impersonation not built operator-auth.ts

    Cyprus-anchored (GDPR + Cyprus DP Law 125(I)/2018), pending counsel review before production. The 7-year figure is the Cyprus statutory limitation period for tax/contract claims; the converted/unconverted split, the pseudonymise_buyer_record() spec and the amendment history live in offplan's ADR 0004 (audit-log retention) — ask for it rather than trusting this table if you are implementing any of them.

    Overview

    route/

    What it is. The home inbox. A KPI strip (total clients; collected / failed payments this month; past-due count), a morning summary (new signups + domain issues in the last 24h), the activation funnel (signed-up → verified → project → assets → published, with trial→paid conversion), and the attention inbox — studios grouped by action-type (payment failed / domain issues / cancelling soon / quiet-but-paying / trials closing / unverified email / stalled onboarding / healthy). A recent-signups rail and a recent operator-activity feed round it out.

    Actions.

    • Resend link (on an unverified-email row) → resends the verification email; the row updates and the action is logged to audit.
    • Funnel drop-count (e.g. "−12 lost →") → scrolls to and highlights the inbox group holding those studios. No change to data — a navigation aid.
    • Studio / signup row links, KPI "Collected" & "Failed" tiles, chargeback & failed- payment banners → navigate to the relevant studio hub or to Payments. Read-only jumps.

    ⚠️ Read the funnel as five independent milestones, not as a funnel. The screen calls it one and the steps are drawn in a row, but each step is its own yes/no over the whole population — a studio can satisfy a later one without the earlier one, so a step can legitimately outrun the step above it. The usual case: a Starter project publishes without any gallery upload, so Published runs ahead of Assets. That is not a counting bug and not a data error, and the "−N lost" figure between two such steps is not a loss. Renaming this strip is group C item 11 of the rebuild spec; until an agency does it, the caveat lives here.

    (Known naming drift, 2026-08-16: this screen's KPI tile still says "Failed" while Payments renamed the same figure "Written off" in its August vocabulary pass — the number is computed the same way; only the word lags. Flagged for the copy sweep.)

    Studios

    route/studios

    What it is. The full studios directory — a filterable table of every studio with verify-state, plan/billing-state, health, run-rate, project count, onboarding state, signed-up and last-active dates, and signup source. Column headers stick while you scroll and the studio-name column is frozen (see chrome in Terms). A studio with zero projects shows "<slug> · no address yet" instead of a synthesised address that has never resolved. A lapsed studio's health badge names its restore deadline: "Subscription ended — restorable until 28 Aug 2026" (from the recorded grace stamp).

    Actions.

    • Filter chips (All / Active / Trial / Suspended / Churned / Deleted), tag filter, search → narrow the table client-side. No data change.
    • Export CSV → downloads the currently-visible rows.
    • +7d trial (row action on trial studios) → extends that studio's trial by 7 days; the row refetches with the new expiry and the button shows "✓ +7d". Logged to audit. (Same underlying action as the hub's Extend trial — this is just the quick fixed-7-day shortcut; the hub modal lets you pick 3 / 7 / 14 / 30.)
    • Studio name → opens that studio's hub. Refresh icon (domain-stuck rows) → jumps to the studio's Domains tab (where Force re-check lives).

    What a shared link carries. ?filter= and ?tag= — a deleted tag in a pasted link reads tag "…" no longer exists — showing the default view rather than erroring.

    Studio hub — Overview

    route/studios/:slug

    The two manager confirm-modals that live in the Actions section:

    What it is. The index tab of the per-studio hub shell (StudioHubLayout, with the 8 tabs across the top). Shows health-alert badges, a KPI grid (Projects, Sign-ins (7d), Run-rate — list price /mo, ex tax), the studio's details, a tag assigner, its live projects, and a 5-step onboarding checklist. The heavy actions live in an Actions section here. On a lapsed studio the health alert names the restore deadline ("Subscription ended — restorable until <date>").

    Reading the "Free trial" detail row. Each account gets one free 14-day trial, and whether it has had it is a recorded fact, not a guess from its project count — so the row answers the question a "can I have another trial?" ticket actually turns on. Three states:

    Row says Means What you can promise
    Available — never granted No trial has ever been granted on this account. It can start one by creating a project; nothing to do.
    Spent · date · Observed We watched the grant happen at that instant. The refusal is on solid ground — quote the date.
    Spent · date · Asserted · backfill The date was filled in retroactively for an account older than the record. Weaker grounds. Don't argue the date with the customer.
    Spent · date · Source unrecorded Something outside the normal path wrote it. Check the audit log before refusing or restoring.
    Not recorded for this studio Demo fixture, or a payload older than this field. Nothing — this is "we don't know", not "available".

    ⚠️ Restoring a spent trial is NOT a control on this screen. The lever exists (POST /api/operator/trial/eligibility, manager-only, audited) but has no button yet, the same way trial/set doesn't — run it from the browser console. offplan holds a runbook for it, which also lists the three questions to ask before saying yes.

    Actions.

    • Tab nav (Overview / Projects / Subscription & Billing / Domains / Users / Activity / Status / Notes) → in-hub navigation. Three of the eight carry an attention mark, so you can see what needs doing before clicking:
      Tab Mark What it means
      Domains a count Custom domains of this studio that are failed, or pending past 24h. Delegated to the Domains console's own predicate, so the tab and the rows behind it cannot disagree.
      Subscription & Billing a dot, not a number Something on that tab needs acting on — chiefly a scheduled cancellation, which appears nowhere else on the hub. "Past due" is a per-studio yes/no, and a badge reading "1" would be theatre.
      Status a count Incidents still open for this studio, over the full retention — not the 24-hour feed the Status tab renders. A badge built on the feed would clear itself at the 24-hour mark whether or not anyone fixed anything.

      A mark you see is a mark you can clear. None of the three is an inventory total — the grey counts (Studios 13 · Domains 26) were pulled off the sidebar in August for exactly that reason, one of them sitting beside a page reading "0 need attention". All three render nothing at zero; a badge that cannot reach zero gets read once and then never again.

    • View live → → opens the studio's public site in a new tab. Rendered only when the studio has an address (first project creates the subdomain); otherwise the Slug row reads "Console key only — no address yet". Inside the ~18s settle window after provisioning or a rename, the link probes readiness server-side first (the console's own CSP forbids probing from the browser) and holds the click with "Not answering from here yet…" until the address answers; a plain copy-link or modifier-click always passes through untouched.
    • + Tag → pick a tag → assigns a pool tag to the studio; the pill appears immediately. × on a tag pill → unassigns it. Both logged.
    • Extend trial → opens a modal with a days picker (3 / 7 / 14 / 30); Confirm adds the days and the trial banner updates.
    • Suspend (manager-only) → a two-step modal: pick a category + optional note, then a confirm screen showing the blast radius (how many projects go dark, how many are PAID); "Freeze studio" suspends it. Resume (manager-only, appears when suspended) → shows the freeze reason on file and un-suspends. All logged.
    • Delete (manager-only, real accounts only) → a confirm modal that requires typing the owner email and a reason (stored in the audit row). This is a soft-delete, not a teardown: it stamps a tombstone, the studio goes dark to its owner and buyers, and projects, media and the subdomain all survive until the purge. You stay on the hub so the DELETED state and the Restore lever are in front of you. The route 409s unless the account is already frozen (suspend-first, ADR 0040) — the modal tells you to freeze it first. The grace window is 30 days benign / 7 days abuse, taken from the freeze category. The done screen names the restore deadline; deleting an already-deleted studio says "Nothing changed" and opens no new grace window.
    • Restore (cs-tier — CS as well as managers; appears on a tombstoned studio) → cancels the pending purge and returns the studio to frozen, not live. Data intact.
    • Purge now (manager-only; appears on a tombstoned or frozen studio) → skips the window and runs the irreversible teardown immediately: projects, subdomains, media, and the account row. Requires typing the owner email + a reason, like Delete. The confirm pane is explicit about what follows: the teardown counts (N projects), the email's fate (see below), that the scheduled purge date is being skipped, and that this is an operational purge, not a complete GDPR Art. 17 erasure — the audit trail and the suppression hash survive by design. The nightly cron does the same thing to anything past its purge date. 409 if the account is neither frozen nor deleted; a partial failure names what was torn down and what is still standing, and is safe to retry. ⚠️ If the freeze category was ToS violation or Fraud suspected, the purge also writes a permanent suppression record, and every later signup on that email is refused silently. The done screen states the email's actual fate as the server recorded it — "blocked from signing up permanently" vs "can sign up again" — rather than re-deriving it from the category you remember picking. There is no un-block lever in this console — removing one is a manual database operation. Check the freeze reason before purging an account you only meant to close.
    • Login as / Password reset → STUB (disabled, Phase-2).

    Studio hub — Projects

    route/studios/:slug/projects

    What it is. The studio's projects as expandable cards — status, visibility, PIN gate, frozen state, theme, stats, and a Features grid (the server-owned FEATURE_REGISTRY: "Live now" features are real on/off toggles gating /dash navigation; "Coming soon" show inert markers).

    Actions.

    • Expand / collapse a card → shows its stats + features + detail rows. No data change.
    • Freeze / Resume (card header) (manager-only) → freezes or resumes a single project; the card re-derives its frozen state. Logged.
    • Feature toggles (manager-only to change) → flip a Live-now feature on/off in the grid (local until saved). Save → a confirm modal lists which features go off + an optional reason; saving persists them, updates the "last changed" line, and logs it. Reset to all On → resets the grid locally (no save until you press Save).

    Studio hub — Billing

    route/studios/:slug/billing

    What it is. The studio's real Stripe billing (TEST-mode today), in one of four states: not-configured (no Stripe key), pre-billing (no customer yet), error (Stripe read failed — quoted, and explicitly distinguished from pre-billing), or ok: subscription rows + card + TRN (UAE tax registration number — an artefact of the sandbox Stripe account's country; revisit at the live Cyprus cutover) + an invoice table (Number · Date · Billed · Collected · Status · PDF · Refund).

    How to read it.

    • Subscription statuses are humanised — Active / On trial / Payment overdue / Cancelled / Unpaid / Never completed / Abandoned at checkout / Paused — never raw Stripe codes.
    • The period-end field says what is true: Renews (live), Ends (cancelling at period end), or Ended (dead — "no further charges"). A cancelled subscription never renders a future date under "Renews".
    • Invoice statuses: Paid / Pending / Failed / Trial $0 / Refunded / Part refunded. When the page cap bites it says "Latest N shown · older invoices are in Stripe".
    • A refunded invoice does not stop being a paid one. Stripe never walks invoice.amount_paid back and never moves the invoice off paid, so the Collected column keeps showing what cleared and the refund is printed beside it as −$900.00, never netted into it. A full refund rendered as $0 would be indistinguishable from an invoice nobody ever paid. The status is what changes: Refunded when the whole amount went home, Part refunded while any of it is still ours.
    • Not here deliberately: the failure reason, next-retry date and hosted pay link live on the cross-studio Payments console, not on this tab.

    Actions.

    • Invoice PDF → opens the invoice PDF (when Stripe provides one).
    • Refund (finance tier — super_admin / admin / finance) → opens a dialog for that one invoice: an amount in USD (leave it blank to refund everything still refundable) and a required reason. Confirm issues a real Stripe refund and the row re-reads with the new status and figure. The link appears only while money is still refundable — a $0 trial invoice and a fully refunded one both have nothing left to give back, so neither shows it. CS can read this tab and cannot move money; a role without billing.view (marketing) gets a 403 screen with no retry button.
      • The reason is required because of what the log would otherwise say. A refund taken in the Stripe dashboard still reaches us — charge.refunded writes a billing.invoice.refunded row — but that row holds no actor and no reason, and an unexplained refund is indistinguishable from an operator error to whoever has to tell them apart later. Refunding here writes two audit rows: the staff action, and the webhook's own row when Stripe confirms.
      • It cannot be undone, the dialog says so, and the server does the arithmetic: the figure in the dialog is context only, so a partial refund that landed while the page was open cannot make you over-refund.
      • Refusals are quoted in plain words — wrong role, invoice belongs to another customer (refused and logged), nothing collected, Stripe unreachable.

    Studio hub — Domains

    route/studios/:slug/domains

    What it is. Per project: the default <slug>.offplan.online subdomain (+ its rename cooldown), any custom domain with live status (pending-DNS / pending-SSL / active / failed), and the previous-address history (redirect → tombstone → released for renames; deactivated rows for disconnected customs).

    Actions.

    • Re-check (pending/failed custom domain) → re-runs the DNS/SSL check; the status updates on refetch. Logged.
    • Rename (subdomain rename control) → a form (new slug + a reason, ≥4 chars); renaming switches the slug, sets the rename cooldown, and retires the old slug (301 → 410). Logged.

    There is no Disconnect here — the disconnected/deactivated rows on this tab are a read-only archive. To actually disconnect a connected custom domain, use the cross-studio Domains console (that's the only place the Disconnect action lives).

    Studio hub — Users

    route/studios/:slug/users

    What it is. The studio's user roster — name, email, status (active / pending / inactive), last login, signup date, owner badge, project count.

    Actions. None — read-only on this tab. User mutations live on the cross-studio Studio users console.

    Studio hub — Activity

    route/studios/:slug/activity

    What it is. The audit timeline scoped to this one studio — freeze/resume, trial extends, domain changes, etc., newest first, with PII-stripped metadata and the actor.

    Actions. None — read-only. It refreshes automatically when a freeze/extend action on this studio fires (shared audit cache tag).

    Studio hub — Status

    route/studios/:slug/status

    What it is. The support-triage view for THIS studio — what broke in its app over the last 24h. Product incidents (logIncident() events recorded in sales-app: upload failures, project create/publish errors, custom-domain failures, auth/billing/email faults) plus an uptime strip for the studio's surfaces. Keyed by the studio owner email (the incident tenant column), not the slug. The counterpart to the cross-studio Status board. Distinct from the Activity tab: Activity is what staff did, Status is what broke.

    Actions. None — read-only, for triage when a studio contacts support. Data is GET /api/operator/status/incidents?studio={ownerEmail}&hours=24 + uptime; it refreshes on mount/arg change (writes come from the studio's own app traffic, not operator mutations).

    Studio hub — Notes

    route/studios/:slug/notes

    What it is. Internal notes on the studio. STUB — no backend; shows an honest "ported in a later increment" notice.

    Actions. None (stub screen).

    Studio users

    route/studio-users

    What it is. The cross-studio user directory — every user flattened across all studios, with their studio, project count, owner/pending state, status, last login, and signup date. Filters (All / Active / Pending / Inactive) + search over name/email/studio. Rows sort by last login, newest first, never-signed-in last — "never signed in" is a separate fact from "longest ago". The sort is fixed, not toggleable.

    Actions.

    • Filter chips + search → narrow the list client-side. The status filter travels in the URL (?status=).
    • View (active users) → jumps to that user's studio Users tab.
    • Resend (pending rows) → resends the verification email (same lever as Overview's).

    Payments

    route/payments

    What it is. The cross-studio payments console (states: not-configured / degraded / ok). When ok: KPI tiles (net MRR / net ARR / collected gross with refunds / written off + past-due / active studios + VAT / open chargebacks), a month switcher, a filterable transaction ledger, and an open-chargebacks table (soonest-deadline first, at-risk highlighted). Subscription/MRR data is live; chargebacks completeness is "verify live" — the earlier conform-audit had these fixture-backed.

    The ledger's vocabulary — six states, and "failed" is not one of them. Each Stripe invoice state carries its own pill and its own one-line meaning: Paid (collected), Awaiting payment (the only state Stripe can still collect on), Not issued (never sent — nobody has been asked for this money), Written off (the only state counted as lost revenue), Cancelled (cancelled before billing — never owed, and not a loss), Refunded. Cancelled is deliberately not in the error palette. The "Written off" KPI tile sums uncollectible only — it used to add cancelled invoices and report thousands "lost" that nobody was ever billed for.

    What the table opens on. Billed — not All. Cancelled and not-issued rows are hidden by default but disclosed, not removed: "N never billed — show" beside the row count switches to All, and a second independent "N $0 / trial hidden — show" reveals zero-value rows. The footer totals one row per currency and per status bucket, each with its meaning line — there is no merged "Total".

    Actions.

    • Month ← → → refetches the ledger for that period.
    • Studio filter, status chips (Billed / All / Paid / Awaiting payment / Written off / Refunded / Cancelled / Not issued), date-range, $0 toggle → narrow the ledger.
    • On an awaiting-payment row: the failure reason and Stripe's own next-retry line ("Stripe retries in Nd" / "…was due Nd ago") render under the status pill; Copy pay link copies Stripe's hosted invoice page (only shown where it can work); Stripe ↗ deep-links the invoice. There is deliberately no retry button — the design is "send them a page they can pay on".
    • Transaction studio link → opens that studio's hub.
    • Respond in Stripe (chargeback row) → opens the Stripe dispute deep-link in a new tab.

    What a shared link carries. Studio, status chip and the $0 toggle — never the month or a day range; a shared link always opens on the current month, and the screen says so.

    Known limitation — "Unlinked" transactions. A ledger row is attributed to a studio only when its Stripe customer id matches a users.stripe_customer_id whose email is that studio's owner (users[0]). The match is deliberately exact — never fuzzy: a mis-attributed money row is a cross-tenant leak, so an unmatched row is shown as Unlinked rather than guessed onto the nearest tenant. This is a standing population, not an incident: it was 38 rows at the 2026-07-30 walkthrough and 37 on 2026-08-17, and it will keep moving — read the current figure off the ledger rather than off this sentence. Expected causes are Stripe customers with no current studio (deleted/reset studios, test-mode customers) and customers held by a non-owner user of an existing studio. The revenue KPIs above the ledger are computed from subscriptions, not from this attribution, so they are unaffected. Not a defect to fix in the console: closing it means backfilling the customer↔studio join, not loosening the match.

    Read-only console — no money is moved from here.

    Domains

    route/domains

    What it is. The cross-studio domain namespace — every project's subdomain (+ rename history: redirect → tombstone → released per ADR 0028), connected custom domains with live status, and disconnected archives. A stats bar (active / pending / failed / stuck / tombstoned / deactivated), filter chips, search, an attention banner, and a per-row drawer (DNS records, vhost, timeline, project/owner links).

    Actions.

    • Filter chips + search → narrow the namespace client-side.
    • Row → drawer → opens the domain's detail (DNS/vhost/history) + its action buttons.
    • Re-check / Disconnect (drawer, custom domains) and Rename (drawer, subdomains) → same effects as on the studio Domains tab, from the cross-studio view. All logged.
    • Project / owner links (drawer) → navigate to the studio hub or its Users tab.

    Activity

    route/activity

    What it is. The cross-studio client activity feed — client logins and self-service changes across all studios, newest first. Each row carries a soft-toned category pill (SIGN-IN, VISIBILITY, PROJECT, …), the action, the studio and project it happened in, a one-line detail, the actor's email with browser/OS, and a right-aligned timestamp. The actor email is shown next to the studio name except when the studio has no name of its own and already renders as that email — then it isn't repeated. Wired to GET /api/operator/activity, 25 rows per page.

    Client events only — deliberately. Staff actions live solely in the Audit log below. Activity shipped with an operator/client source toggle at first ratification, and the live review dropped it: operator rows duplicated the Audit log, and the category filter — a client-event concept — silently did nothing when source=operator, which read as broken data. One clear job per screen, zero duplication, and the category filter now always applies. The backend keeps the source param, defaulting to client.

    Actions.

    • Studio typeahead → filters to one tenant. Options come from the complete studios payload rather than the loaded page, so every studio stays selectable regardless of which ones happen to appear in the current events.
    • Category dropdown → All plus the five curated client categories (mirrors the CLIENT_EVENT_CATEGORIES set in sales-app).
    • Load more → keyset pagination; already-shown pages are retained and the next page is appended. The cursor does not travel in the URL (unlike Audit's).
    • Studio name in a row footer → jumps to that studio's hub Activity tab.

    What a shared link carries. ?studio=<slug> and ?category= — the studio is identified by slug, never by the owner's email. A link with a studio filter waits for the slug pool before rendering, so it never flashes unfiltered rows.

    Read-only — zero DB writes, and no raw ip in the payload.

    Not to be confused with the per-studio hub Activity tab (/studios/:slug/activity), which shows a single studio's merged operator + client timeline.

    Audit

    route/audit

    What it is. The cross-studio action log — every tenant's audit events, newest first: area badge (severity-coloured), action, tenant, an actor badge (see below), PII tier, description, timestamp, and an expandable actor/payload detail. Server-side filters + keyset pagination.

    The actor badge — who did it, and which era the row belongs to. Every row carries the actor in a mono badge (dark only when the actor is staff), and its kind is a stored fact (actor_type, migration 0059), not guessed from the email shape: operator (staff), customer (the studio's own session), system (webhook / cron), or unattributed — pre-cutover row for rows written before the column existed. The header states the two seal eras explicitly: rows sealed before 15 Aug 2026 commit to ten fields with tenant and actor kind outside the seal; rows sealed since commit to those too. A verification line under the header shows the nightly chain check: ✓ Chain intact as of <ts> · N rows walked, or a red CHAIN BROKEN banner naming the first mismatching row — escalate before acting on the log if you see it.

    Actions.

    • Tenant typeahead → filters to one tenant, server-side. Options include tenants that survive only in the log — those render as <email> (not in Studios).
    • Action dropdown → All actions, seven groups (Studios / Projects / Access / Tags / Domains / Billing / Operators), or a single code. A group header is itself an option: picking Billing — all filters to every billing action in one click. *.view codes are deliberately unfilterable noise-guards.
    • Actor dropdown → Everyone or one actor (includes stripe:webhook and cron).
    • Date range From / To, with a single ✕ clearing both.
    • Prev / Next → keyset pagination through pages.
    • Row expand → reveals the raw action code, the actor email + kind label, tenant, time, and the full payload JSON.

    What a shared link carries. The action filter, the dates and the page cursor travel in the URL; the tenant and actor filters do not (both are email addresses, and an address must not travel in a URL) — the screen says so whenever either is set. A link-seeded page labels itself "Linked page" rather than guessing an ordinal.

    Read-only — the audit log is a record, never edited.

    Status

    route/status

    What it is. The cross-studio «Status» board — the morning "where's it burning" glance. Product incidents across ALL studios in the last 24h (newest first), a systemic-signal strip that groups incidents by kind and flags any kind spanning ≥2 distinct studios (so a platform-wide fault — e.g. R2 down → many upload failures — reads differently from one studio's isolated error), and an uptime strip. This is what broke; the Audit console is what staff did. Per-studio detail lives in the studio-hub Status tab.

    Open vs cleared. Only open incidents carry severity colour, escalation advice and a place in the systemic-signal strip. A cleared incident folds into a collapsible "N cleared" row (the fold state travels in the URL as ?resolved=) and reads "Cleared <date> — no action needed. Kept here because this board is a 24-hour log of what broke, not a list of what is open." When everything has cleared the board says "Nothing open — everything logged in the last 24h has cleared."

    Actions.

    • Time window — the board reads the last 24h (GET /api/operator/status/incidents?hours=24, no studio filter).
    • Row → the incident summary, kind, affected studio, and timestamp.
    • N cleared → expands/collapses the cleared incidents.

    Read-only. Layer 2 (status-http-health, CF 4xx/5xx analytics) is deferred pending a Cloudflare Analytics:Read token; the board shows Layer 1 (incident event-log) + Layer 3 (uptime pings) today.

    Operators

    route/operators

    What it is. The staff roster — email, name, role (super_admin / admin / finance / cs / marketing), status, invited-by, and the invite/accept/deactivate dates. Includes the 5-role capability matrix, served from the same constant the server's can() gate reads — there is no second copy to drift. The roster opens on Active (chips All / Active / Pending / Disabled, carried in the URL); when a search matches rows the status filter hides, the empty state says how many and offers show-all. Non-managers see a read-only roster. There is deliberately no delete — the roster is what attributes audit rows.

    Actions.

    • Filter chips + search → narrow the roster client-side.
    • Invite operator (manager-only) → a modal form (email + optional name + role); validates a corporate @offplan.online email and a role, then sends the invite. The invite link is valid for 24 hours. An admin may grant up to admin and no further; only a super-admin mints another super-admin. On success "Invite sent"; friendly error codes cover non-corporate email / already-on-roster / self / super-admin / rate-limited / etc. Logged. ⚠️ Known copy defect (2026-08-16): the Re-send invite modal still says "a fresh 7-day link" — the real lifetime is 24 hours everywhere (the email itself renders from the 24h constant). Flagged for the copy sweep; the guard that caught the other four stale mentions only covered the sales-app sources.
    • Change role (manager-only, per row) → same escalation rule as inviting. Logged.
    • Deactivate (manager-only, per row) → a confirm modal; deactivating disables the operator. Guardrails block deactivating the last super-admin or yourself. Logged.

    Settings

    route/settings

    What it is. The admin reference console. Shows the payment-provider status (real — Stripe connected/test/live vs manual fallback vs not-configured), the studio-tag pool (active + archived, with a live "studios using" count), and data-retention horizons (read-only, ADR-sourced). (Reconciliation note: the earlier conform-audit marked Settings "client-only STUB"; that is now stale — tag CRUD and provider status are wired. The only absent piece is a provider-config form, deferred to Phase 4b.)

    Actions.

    • Create tag (manager-only) → a modal (name + optional description); creating adds it to the active pool. Logged.
    • Archive (manager-only, active tag) → a confirm modal showing how many studios use it; archiving moves it to the archived section and drops it from studios' tag lists.
    • Restore (manager-only, archived tag) → a confirm modal; restoring returns it to the active pool. All logged.

    Data-retention horizons are read-only. No provider-config editing yet (Phase 4b).

    Sign in

    route/signed-out

    What it is. The console's own sign-in screen, and where you land whenever the staff probe fails. Enter your work email and a single-use link is sent to it; there is no password. Until 2026-07-31 this screen had no form at all — sign-in was Cloudflare Access at the edge — so it could only offer a "re-authenticate" link, which does not exist on ops.offplan.online, the ungated host the console moved to on 2026-08-14 (ADR 0047).

    Actions.

    • Email me a sign-in link → sends a link valid once, for 30 minutes.

    What it will never tell you. The reply is identical whether the address is an active operator, a deactivated one, or a stranger — deliberately, so the form cannot be used to discover who has console access. "Check your email" is not confirmation that an account exists.

    Why you were sent here (?reason=, set by the gate, about your own identity only):

    reason Heading Means
    (none) Sign in. No session — the ordinary case.
    deactivated Access revoked. Your account is disabled. A new link will not help — ask a super admin to reactivate you.
    pending Invite not accepted. Open the accept-link in your invitation email; that activates the account and signs you in.
    unavailable Console unavailable. The operator store could not be read, so sign-in is closed rather than guessing. Transient.

    Verify sign-in link

    route/auth/verify

    What it is. Where the emailed link lands. It spends the token, sets the session cookie and drops you into the console — you should only ever see it in passing.

    The emailed URL is a plain page load; the token is only consumed by the request this screen makes after it renders. That split exists because corporate mail scanners prefetch links, and a link that consumed itself on GET would be dead before you clicked it.

    If it says "Link expired." The link has already been used, more than 30 minutes have passed, or the account is no longer active. Request a new link returns you to sign-in.

    See also

    • Index — the map + access rules (read first).
    • Agency rebuild spec — the third document of this set, and the one an incoming agency reads: what exists, what is deliberately unbuilt, and the register of changes to make.
    • Dev ARCHITECTURE.md — apps/operator-panel/ARCHITECTURE.md in the code package — frontend↔/api wiring.
    • Version — each document carries its own doc_version in its frontmatter and page header. They move independently; there is no single version for the set.

    Что это. По разделу на экран: что это, что делает каждое действие и что происходит после. Сначала прочитайте индекс — там карта и правила доступа; здесь подробности. Порядок экранов совпадает с боковой панелью.

    Рамки — возможности, а не политика. Здесь написано, что делает элемент управления и что за этим следует — например, «Extend trial добавляет N дней, и баннер пробного периода у студии обновляется». Здесь не написано, когда вам следует это делать (операционная политика — отдельная, отложенная работа). Там, где действие доступно только управляющим, это обеспечивает сервер, а кнопка просто скрыта у остальных (сокрытие на клиенте — дополнительный рубеж, а не авторитет).

    STUB помечает экран или действие, данные которого являются заглушкой и ещё не подключены к бэкенду — оно рисуется, но не живое.

    О скриншотах. Все двенадцать сняты с живой консоли 2026-08-17, поэтому они совпадают с текстом. Почтовые адреса замаскированы — в консоли живые данные клиентов, а эти страницы опубликованы открыто; operator1@offplan.online и studio-owner1@example.com являются подстановками, применёнными единообразно. Слаги студий не маскируются: они и так публичны как <slug>.offplan.online.

    О переводе. Это перевод английского плейбука, сделанный по глоссарию перевода (внутренний документ offplan). Названия элементов интерфейса оставлены по-английски — вы будете искать глазами именно их: кнопка называется Refund, а не «Возврат». Идентификаторы, роли, маршруты и коды действий не переводятся никогда. При расхождении с оригиналом прав оригинал: он является источником, а этот файл — снимком с него на версии, указанной в шапке.

    Машиночитаемых комментариев route:, которые есть в английском файле, здесь нет намеренно: их сверяет с router.tsx проверка на устаревание (scripts/check_docs_screens.py), и вторая копия была бы вторым источником расхождений.

    Термины и обозначения

    Повторяющийся словарь, определённый один раз. Просмотрите перед таблицами ниже.

    Статус данных (правая колонка везде):

    Метка Что означает
    WIRED Реальные данные — экран запрашивает и показывает живые значения.
    PARTIAL В основном реальные, но одна часть всё ещё выводится или является заглушкой (указано по экрану).
    STUB Заглушка — рисуется, но данные или действие ещё не подключены к бэкенду.
    Phase-2 Элемент управления, который виден, но намеренно отключён — ещё не построен (не сломан).

    Остальное:

    • обвязка (chrome) — неподвижная рамка вокруг каждого экрана (верхняя панель + боковая панель + командная строка); сама по себе не экран. Липкая с 2026-08-15: верхняя и боковая панели остаются на виду на любой глубине прокрутки, а шапки колонок таблиц прилипают под верхней панелью — если только таблица не слишком широка, и тогда она переходит в горизонтальную прокрутку с замороженной колонкой идентификатора, так что ни одна колонка не становится недостижимой и ни одна строка не теряет своё имя.
    • плашка — маленькая скруглённая метка состояния (например, TRIAL, PAID, точка состояния).
    • Одноразовая ссылка (magic link) — как вы входите. Вы вводите рабочий email на экране Sign in, проходите проверку Turnstile, и на почту приходит одноразовая ссылка, действующая 30 минут; переход по ней начинает сессию. Поля пароля нет, и кнопки SSO нет — учётными данными служит сам email. Решение за сессией — ADR 0048 у offplan; ADR 0047 — отдельное, про хост, на который она переехала.
    • CF Access (Cloudflare Access) — отменён 2026-07-31. До этого консоль стояла за Cloudflare Access, и вход происходил на границе сети, до загрузки приложения. Ничто в консоли больше так не работает — поиск cf-access / CF_Authorization по apps/operator-panel/src/app/ не находит ничего. Термин остаётся здесь только для того, чтобы можно было прочитать старый документ, ADR или сообщение коммита, где он упоминается; если вы ищете вход через SSO, его нет.
    • ADR — запись об архитектурном решении (заметки «почему мы сделали так» в docs/decisions/). Когда экран говорит «по ADR 00NN», это правило, стоящее за поведением. Файлы ADR с этим набором не едут, поэтому те, на которые ссылается код консоли, — здесь:
      • 0003 — soft-suspend обратим; hard-delete — это GDPR-стирание.
      • 0004 — хранение аудита и записей покупателей: 12 месяцев, дальше личности акторов хешируются (этой джобы пока нет).
      • 0028 — политика переименования субдомена и валидация slug.
      • 0031 — структура цен. Коммерчески вне объёма переписывания.
      • 0034 — таксономия тегов студии.
      • 0040 — governance удаления: сначала suspend, и guarded delete — не стирание.
      • 0048 — своя сессия консоли на своём хосте (см. Magic link выше).
      • 0049 — что разрешено, решает сервер, а не панель (can() против ACTION_ROLES).
      • 0051 — неоплата: страница гаснет в конце периода, окно восстановления закрывается по производной.
    • MRR / ARR — месячная и годовая регулярная выручка (KPI по подписочной выручке на Payments).
    • постраничная навигация по ключу — просто Назад / Вперёд постранично (без перехода на номер). Механизм вам не нужен, нужны только кнопки.
    • tombstone / 301 → 410 — отставленный адрес, оставленный в записях после переименования: сначала он редиректит 301 (переехал) на новый, затем становится 410 gone. Показывается в истории домена.
    • PII / псевдонимизация / уровень PII — PII = персональные данные. «Уровень PII» помечает, насколько чувствительно записываемое поле, и чувствительные поля вырезаются из метаданных до записи. Псевдонимизация — это план, а не состояние: ADR 0004 говорит, что личности акторов через 12 месяцев становятся хешем, а задачи, которая это сделала бы, не существует — каждый актор в журнале хранится и показывается открытым текстом независимо от возраста (audit.ts:6-8).
    • Copy view link — элемент управления на всех восьми списочных консолях (Studios, Operators, Status, Studio users, Activity, Domains, Payments, Audit), который копирует текущий отфильтрованный вид как абсолютный URL. То, что фильтры каждого экрана кладут в URL, является поверхностью совместимости — параметры добавляют, но не переименовывают (авторитетная таблица по экранам лежит в ARCHITECTURE.md панели оператора). Значения по умолчанию в URL не пишутся. Надписи: Copy view link → Link copied (или Could not copy — use the address bar).
    • уведомление об устаревшем параметре — когда во вставленной ссылке приходит значение, которого экран больше не знает (удалённый тег, отменённый фильтр), экран показывает вид по умолчанию и говорит об этом одним предложением (например, tag "vip" no longer exists — showing the default view), а не падает с ошибкой и не выбрасывает значение молча.
    • возврат на исходный экран — ссылка на консоль, которой поделились и которая потребовала входа, этот вход переживает: назначение сохраняется локально (60 минут, используется один раз), и верификация одноразовой ссылки возвращает вас ровно на тот отфильтрованный вид. Это не параметр ?next= — в письме о назначении не путешествует ничего.
    • /dash — собственный кабинет студии (отдельная поверхность, не эта консоль — см. индекс).
    • FEATURE_REGISTRY — фиксированный серверный каталог функций продукта, из которого берутся переключатели «Features grid» на вкладке Projects.
    • зона поражения (blast radius) — на подтверждении заморозки: сколько всего затронет действие — сколько проектов уйдёт в офлайн и сколько из них на платных тарифах.
    • «уйти в офлайн» / заморозка — публичная страница продаж замороженного проекта перестаёт отдаваться покупателям, пока проект не разморозят.

    Все экраны

    Сверенный хребет — каждый экран, его маршрут, React-компонент и файл за ним, и являются ли данные реальными (WIRED) или заглушкой (STUB). Каждая строка разворачивается в полноценный раздел ниже. Источником правды является роутер (apps/operator-panel/src/app/router.tsx); эта таблица сверена с ним (последний раз 2026-08-17), а проверка на устаревание ловит любое расхождение.

    Одна дата, а не три. last_reviewed в шапке — единственное утверждение о свежести, которое делает этот документ. Даты внутри датированных заметок ниже — это история того, как он сюда пришёл; читайте их как «что произошло в тот день», а не как «насколько это свежо».

    router.tsx объявляет 24 узла с элементами = 21 конечный экран + 2 обёртки-layout + 1 предохранитель аутентификации. Layout — это обвязка, а не экраны: OperatorLayout (/ — оболочка с верхней панелью, боковой панелью и CommandBar, описана в индексе) и StudioHubLayout (studios/:slug — оболочка для 8 вкладок хаба студии; оставлена строкой ниже для контекста). OperatorAuthGate тоже несёт элемент и раньше не учитывался — так этот абзац и оказался с числом 21 при роутере, объявляющем 24. Пути даны относительно базового /operator-next. /signed-out и /auth/verify публичны по необходимости — они работают до того, как появляется личность; всё, что ниже, закрыто OperatorAuthGate по куке op_admin_session, и только по ней (см. ADR 0048 у offplan; заголовка CF Access, который это предложение называло раньше, как способа входа не существует с 2026-07-31).

    ⚠️ У одного из конечных экранов ниже намеренно нет метки route:. NotFoundRoute (path: "*", router.tsx:104) исключён самой проверкой на устаревание (check_docs_screens.py:221-224 — перехватывающий маршрут рисует запасную страницу 404, а не документируемый экран), поэтому метка для него сделала бы проверку красной у документа, который стал полнее. Ему положена строка в таблице и не положен раздел. Именно поэтому проверка сообщает 20 маршрутов / 20 меток при 21 конечном экране.

    Маршрут Компонент Исходник (.../routes/) Что это Данные
    /signed-out SignedOutRoute signed-out.tsx Публичный. Экран входа — спрашивает email и запрашивает одноразовую ссылку. WIRED
    /auth/verify AuthVerifyRoute auth-verify.tsx Публичный. Куда приходит ссылка из письма; тратит токен и начинает сессию. WIRED

    /studios StudiosRoute studios.tsx Каталог студий — фильтруемая таблица, продление пробного периода. WIRED
